text:
Mother, when I am grown,
oh, what a strapping lad you'll have!
I'll lift you in my arms,
as the zonda lifts the grass.


Or I'll lay you on the haystacks,
or carry you all the way to the sea,
or take you up the hills,
or leave you on the threshold.


And what a little home will
your little boy, your giant, build for you,
and what loving shade
its eaves will give?


I'll water you a garden,
and tire your skirt out
with fruit and more fruit,
a thousand kinds and more.


Or better, I'll make you tapestries
from rushes for weaving;
or better, I'll own a mill
to talk to you as it makes bread.


Count, count the windows
and the doors of the house;
count, count the wonders,
if you can count them…

translation.title: Mother, When I Am Grown...
